title: Smc5/6 uses its head-NSE module to preferentially associate with ssDNA gaps and ss-dsDNA junctions.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the complete Europe PMC supplementary package (1.44 MB): it contains only 8 figure images (JPG/GIF) plus one 12,134-character supplemental PDF, whose extracted text has no tables at all (figure panels only). I grepped the open-access full text for every sample size and found only N = 15, 41, 50 and 79. The data availability statement reads 'All study data are included in the article and/or supporting information.' A Zenodo/Dryad/Figshare search on the DOI returned nothing, and the only accessions anywhere in the text are other papers' PDB structures (7YQH, 8I13, 8T8E, 7TVE).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experimental details (atomic force microscopy imaging conditions, DNA substrate construction, protein purification) and the claim that gapping efficiency was 90.5% +/- 4.8% come from the methods text; I could not check any per-molecule measurement because none is distributed.

a1_downloadable.note: No dataset exists to download. The entire supplement is figure images plus a figure-only PDF; the data availability statement says all data are 'included in the article', meaning the raw atomic force microscopy (AFM) images and the per-molecule measurements behind every plot were never deposited. Verified by unzipping the supplement and extracting the PDF text.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no column anywhere. Any label (binding position along the DNA, which protein module contacts the DNA, measured height or volume) would have to be reconstructed by re-measuring pixels off published figure images, i.e. constructed from scratch.

a3_inputs_present.note: The model inputs would be the raw AFM height maps; these are not provided in any machine-readable form, only as rendered JPG/GIF figure panels with overlaid annotations and scale bars.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are clearly stated in the text and figure axes (nanometres for height and contour length, kDa for estimated molecular weight, percent of contour length for binding position) — but they label figures, not a data file.

a5_enough_rows.note: The largest reported sample is N = 79 protein-DNA complexes (others are N = 41, N = 50, N = 15 preparations). That is two orders of magnitude below the ~1,500-row bar, and these counts are from the figure legends, not a file.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small — but only because the supplement is 19 image files and a PDF with nothing to model.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be assessed: there is no download to compare against the paper's counts, which is itself the failure.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean in principle — binding positions and heights are direct AFM measurements of purified yeast Smc5/6 on defined DNA substrates, not another model's output. The problem is quantity and availability, not circularity.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper distributes no measurements, only figures, so no model can be trained or evaluated on this work.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use microscope images of protein-DNA complexes to predict where a repair protein binds along a DNA molecule.
plain_idea.train_on: The intended input was atomic force microscopy (AFM) height images of single Smc5/6 protein complexes sitting on defined DNA molecules — a microscope that traces surface height at nanometre scale. Verified example count: at most 79 complexes in the largest experiment, and none are distributed as data.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be the binding site along the DNA (single-stranded gap, single-to-double-stranded junction, or flanking double-stranded DNA) and which part of the complex makes the contact. Truth comes from a human expert tracing each AFM image by hand.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Automating AFM image tracing would help the handful of labs doing single-molecule DNA-repair imaging, and in principle would remove the subjectivity of manual particle scoring. With tens of hand-scored molecules and no image files released, none of that is reachable from this paper.

ml_idea: Considered and discarded: an image model that scores AFM height maps to classify where Smc5/6 binds a DNA substrate and which structural module makes the contact, replacing manual particle tracing. Dead on arrival because the raw images are not deposited and the hand-scored sample is tens of molecules.

effort.compute_note: Only the 1.44 MB supplement zip was handled; no modelling workload was estimated because there is no data to model.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Unzip the supplement and list its contents — it takes one minute and shows 19 figure images and one figure-only PDF, with zero tabular or image data files.

verdict_reason: No data is distributed at all — the supplement is figure images plus a figure-only PDF, with the data availability statement saying everything is 'in the article' — and the largest experiment scores just 79 single molecules by hand, so A1, A2, A3, A5 and A7 all fail.
